copy.headline: How two Democrats took Republican-controlled Arlington House seats
copy.caption:
A political science professor said the wins had many factors, from top-of-the-ballot strength to affordability and growing diversity. The year 1969 was marked by historic moments for the United States: The first man walked on the moon, young men faced the first military draft of the Vietnam War and hippies converged on upstate New York for Woodstock.

Down south, another milestone quietly unfolded. The year marked the last time Democrats would simultaneously hold Texas House Districts 94 and 96.

story.title: How two Democrats took Republican-controlled Arlington House seats
story.summary: A political science professor said the wins had many factors, from top-of-the-ballot strength to affordability and growing diversity. The year 1969 was marked by historic moments for the United States: The first man walked on the moon, young men faced the first military draft of the Vietnam War and hippies converged on upstate New York for Woodstock. Down south, another milestone quietly unfolded. The year marked the last time Democrats would simultaneously hold Texas House Districts 94 and 96. One Republican incumbent left to run for the Tarrant County Commissioners Court, and the other campaigned for Texas Senate, leaving the seats open on Nov. 3. In both districts, Democratic challengers beat their Republican opponents, taking control of the seats that span central and south Arlington.
